qt: to the Commission Leoluca Orlando (Verts/ALE), Nicolae Ștefănuță (Verts/ALE), Estrella Galán (The Left), Mimmo Lucano (The Left), Rudi Kennes (The Left), Cecilia Strada (S&D), Danilo Della Valle (The Left), Alessandro Zan (S&D), Manon Aubry (The Left), Benedetta Scuderi (Verts/ALE), Murielle Laurent (S&D), Sandro Ruotolo (S&D), Ignazio Roberto Marino (Verts/ALE), Marie Toussaint (Verts/ALE), Brando Benifei (S&D), Valentina Palmisano (The Left), Ilaria Salis (The Left), Chloé Ridel (S&D), Vicent Marzà Ibáñez (Verts/ALE), Jaume Asens Llodrà (Verts/ALE), Pasquale Tridico (The Left), Matjaž Nemec (S&D), Tineke Strik (Verts/ALE), Mélissa Camara (Verts/ALE), Sara Matthieu (Verts/ALE), Jussi Saramo (The Left), Tilly Metz (Verts/ALE), Marco Tarquinio (S&D) Subject:

Following the arrival of tens of thousands of people in the Spanish exclave of Ceuta on 30 July 2026, Italy reintroduced controls at air and sea borders with Spain until 16 September, in breach of the Schengen Agreement. This was a disproportionate measure considering that the Commission had declared that there were no movements of persons from Ceuta to Spain or other continental European Member States. Spain responded by introducing controls on arrivals from Italy. Other Member States have announced plans to send back to Italy any migrants whose asylum applications should have been handled there under the Dublin system. The action of the Italian Government risks turning a humanitarian emergency into a clash between Member States, fragmenting the Schengen area and fueling the narrative of the sovereignist far-right that the EU is incapable of acting collectively, while relegating human rights and European solidarity to the margins of political debate. We ask the Commission: 1.
Will it ask Italy to lift its border controls?
What measures will it take to ensure solidarity between Member States, a solidarity Italy has always demanded from the EU during episodes of large-scale immigration?
What measures should be taken to ensure that humanitarianism and the protection of the rights of migrants and refugees remain central to the EU’s response?
